results.description:
'I really think this book might become the sleeper hit of the Christmas rush'. Robert McCrum
'An excellent, compassionate biography of the wildly prolific romantic novelist'. The Guardian
'Sweet writes with great wit and brio but also considerable sympathy'. Observer
'Every page of this biography is a cliff-hanger... jaw-dropping...her extraordinary, tragic life is gripping from start to finish'. The Spectator
'Fantastically enjoyable, drily hilarious and incredibly well-researched'. Literary Review
'Matthew Sweet has given the life-story of this icon of chiffon-and-pearls the telling it deserves - wry, affectionate, and very readable.' Louis Theroux
'Matthew Sweet, who seems born to write this biography, installs us in an open-topped two-seater, and puts his foot down on the gas like a boy racer, hurtling his readers through a no-man's-land of shell shock and party going'. The Tablet
'Sweet's prose is peppered with dry wit and sharpened by an eye for telling detail'. The Telegraph
'A corker of a biography...gives us an outrageously entertaining portrait of a formidable woman'. The Bookseller
'The most genius, compelling, jaw-dropping, access-all-areas biography of Barbara Cartland.' India Knight
'This book is superb. A psychologically acute rendering of a publishing phenomenon.' Jenny Colgan

Penniless virgins. Reckless dukes. Flappers. Airmen. Suffragettes. Barbara Cartland made them fall in love. She wrote 723 books without touching a typewriter: instead, she reclined on her sofa with a Pekinese on her lap - and romantic fiction billowed out of her.

This dazzling biography reveals the woman behind the powder and mascara - a clever, socially precarious writer navigating a twentieth-century world of war-damaged men, class conflict and sexual peril.

After 49 proposals, she chose the wrong one. What followed was a life stranger than any of her novels.

From country house weekends to Fleet Street offices, from Mayfair bedrooms to the divorce court, Matthew Sweet traces Cartland's extraordinary journey through a century of upheaval. Here are terrorist plots, psychic seances, suppressed scandals, plagiarism battles in the cutthroat world of romance publishing - and a surprising turn as a campaigner for Romany rights.

Drawing on unprecedented access to Cartland's vast archives and firsthand accounts from those who knew her, Sweet delivers a wonderfully entertaining study of class, fame, scandal and self-aggrandisement. Part satire, part biography, part social history, The Great Dictator reveals how a literary legend was made.
